Where to go next

If your question is really about stopping, our guide to stopping GLP-1s and keeping the weight off is the long version of the regain and maintenance evidence. If it is about side effects, the semaglutide side-effects guide covers what helps at each step. If it is about cost, the cheapest GLP-1 index and the month 1 vs year one guide carry every verified price. If it is about whether a compounded product is safe, the compounded vs brand-name guide and the 503A vs 503B guide explain how to check the pharmacy. And if you are starting from the beginning, the complete guide to GLP-1 weight loss online is the place to begin. This article is general information, not medical advice; a licensed clinician decides whether any dose of any GLP-1 is appropriate for you.

articles.title: GLP-1 Muscle Loss: How Much You Lose and How to Keep It
articles.description: What the semaglutide and tirzepatide DXA substudies show about lean mass, what bimagrumab changes, and the protein and training that protect muscle.
articles.author: Treatments Hub Research Team
keyTakeaways: In the trials that scanned body composition, lean mass made up roughly 40% of the weight lost on semaglutide (STEP 1 DXA substudy) and about a quarter on tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-1 substudy). Lean mass is not the same as muscle: it includes water, organ tissue and the fat-free part of fat tissue that shrinks with the fat.

Losing some lean mass with large weight loss is normal and happens with diet, surgery and drugs alike. The question is not whether, but how much and whether function keeps up; the SEMALEAN study found strength and function were maintained in its semaglutide group despite lean-mass change.

The two levers with evidence are adequate protein and resistance training, which are also the two things a weekly injection does nothing about. A drug that blocks muscle loss directly (bimagrumab, with semaglutide) reported 93% of weight lost as fat in a phase 2 trial in 2025, but it is not approved and not for sale.
Nobody should reduce or stretch a GLP-1 dose to protect muscle. The label dose and the prescriber's plan stay; muscle is protected at the table and in the gym.

sections.heading: Do GLP-1 medications cause muscle loss?
sections.body:
Key takeaways and quick verdict

Yes, people lose lean mass on semaglutide and tirzepatide, because people lose lean mass with any large weight loss. The scanned substudies put the lean share at about 40% of total loss for semaglutide and about 25% for tirzepatide, and a sizeable part of that "lean" figure is water and the support tissue of fat, not contractile muscle. Strength and physical function were maintained in the one study built to measure them. The practical answer is unglamorous: eat enough protein, lift something heavy twice a week, do not skip meals to speed the scale, and never cut the dose to spare muscle. Sources: STEP 1, NEJM, 2021, SURMOUNT-1, NEJM, 2022, SEMALEAN, 2025, checked October 28, 2026.

The muscle question has become the most-searched objection to GLP-1 treatment, and for a reason: the before-and-after photographs that sell these drugs show smaller bodies, and a smaller body with the same proportion of muscle is a weaker one. The fear is not irrational. It is, however, usually built on the wrong number. This guide sets out what the trials actually measured, what "lean mass" means on a DXA scan, what the one drug designed to prevent the loss showed, and what you can do about it this week without touching your prescription.

Two rules frame everything below. First, all of the body-composition data comes from trial substudies, with scans on a subset of participants, so the numbers are estimates with wide error bars, not laws. Second, nothing here is a reason to change a dose. The labels set the dose and the prescriber adjusts it; the tools for protecting muscle are food and training, and they work at any dose.

sections.heading: What the trials measured, and what 'lean mass' means
sections.body:
Both pivotal weight-loss trials ran a body-composition substudy in which a subset of participants had dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans at baseline and at the end of treatment. DXA divides the body into bone mineral, fat mass and everything else, which it calls lean mass. That third category is the one that gets quoted as "muscle", and it is the source of most of the confusion.

STEP 1: semaglutide 2.4 mg

In STEP 1, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021, the DXA substudy scanned 140 participants over 68 weeks. Fat mass fell by more than lean mass in absolute and proportional terms, but lean mass still accounted for roughly 40% of the total weight lost in the semaglutide group, a figure that secondary analyses have reported at about 39% to 40% depending on the statistical approach. The proportion of lean mass to total body mass went up, because fat fell faster. Source: Wilding et al., NEJM, 2021, checked October 28, 2026.

SURMOUNT-1: tirzepatide

SURMOUNT-1, published in the same journal in 2022, ran a DXA substudy of its own. Its result is the one quoted most favourably for tirzepatide: pooled across doses, lean mass accounted for about a quarter of the weight lost, with fat mass falling by roughly three times as much as lean mass. The difference from STEP 1 is real but should not be over-read, because the substudies differed in size, population and total weight lost, and a trial that loses more weight tends to lose a larger absolute amount of lean tissue even when the proportion is lower. Source: Jastreboff et al., NEJM, 2022, checked October 28, 2026.

What is in the lean number

DXA lean mass is everything that is not bone and not fat: skeletal muscle, yes, but also organ tissue, skin, connective tissue, the blood vessels and stroma that run through fat tissue, and water. When a person loses a large amount of fat, the scaffolding of that fat goes with it and registers as lean loss. When glycogen stores fall, as they do with lower food intake, the water bound to glycogen leaves and registers as lean loss. Neither is muscle fibre. A careful 2026 review of the trial literature makes the point that true skeletal-muscle loss on these drugs is probably smaller than the headline lean figures suggest, while also noting that the trials did not measure muscle directly. Source: Barbell Medicine evidence review, 2026, checked October 28, 2026.

Trial (substudy)DrugScanned participantsLean share of weight lost (as reported)What it does not tell you
STEP 1 DXA substudySemaglutide 2.4 mg, 68 weeks140About 40%How much was muscle versus water and support tissue; strength or function
SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudyTirzepatide 5-15 mg, 72 weeksSubset (see paper)About 25% pooledSame; plus comparability with STEP 1 (different population, larger total loss)
BELIEVE (phase 2b)Bimagrumab + semaglutide, 72 weeks507 enrolledAbout 7% (93% of loss was fat), as reported at ADA 2025Durability, safety at scale; not an approved product
SEMALEANSemaglutide, clinical cohortSmallLean mass changed; strength and function maintainedLong-term outcomes

sections.heading: Is GLP-1 muscle loss worse than losing weight any other way?
sections.body:
Not on the evidence available. Lean loss of a quarter to a third of total weight lost is the long-standing rule of thumb for diet-induced weight loss, and bariatric surgery series report similar or higher proportions. The GLP-1 figures sit inside that range. What the drugs change is scale: more people are losing more weight, faster, and often without a dietitian or a training plan attached, so the absolute amount of lean tissue at stake in the population is larger than it has ever been. That is a reason to take protein and training seriously, not evidence that the drugs are uniquely catabolic.

The one study built to ask whether function suffers found that it did not. SEMALEAN, published in 2025, followed people on semaglutide with measures of muscle strength and physical function alongside body composition. Lean mass changed, as expected; grip strength and function were maintained. It is a small study and it is one study, but it is the right kind of study, and its answer matches what clinicians see: people who lose a lot of weight on these drugs usually move better, not worse, because the load on the muscle they keep has dropped. Source: SEMALEAN, PMC, 2025, checked October 28, 2026.

Who should worry more

Risk is not evenly spread. Adults over about 60, who are already losing muscle each year, people with low muscle mass to begin with, people losing weight very fast, and anyone eating far below their protein needs because the drug has removed their appetite are the groups where lean loss can tip into sarcopenia, the clinical state of low muscle and low function. For them, the section on protein and training below is not optional, and a conversation with the prescriber about rate of loss is reasonable. Our guide to GLP-1 weight loss over 40 covers the age dimension.

sections.heading: How much protein do you need on a GLP-1 to keep muscle?
sections.body:
Protein is the raw material for keeping muscle during a calorie deficit, and GLP-1 drugs make it harder to get enough of it, because they suppress appetite in general rather than appetite for fat and sugar in particular. The common failure is a day of a yoghurt, half a sandwich and a smoothie, which is well under 60 grams of protein for most adults and far below what a body in deficit needs to hold onto muscle.

The floor is the Recommended Dietary Allowance, 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day, which the National Academies set as the amount that prevents deficiency in healthy adults who are not losing weight. It was never designed for someone in a large deficit, and the sports-nutrition and geriatric literature has long argued for more in that situation; the figures clinicians use for people on GLP-1 treatment are above the RDA, and the right target for an individual depends on kidney function, age and body size, which is why the number belongs in a conversation with a dietitian or prescriber rather than in a blanket recommendation here. Source for the RDA: Dietary Reference Intakes, National Academies, checked October 28, 2026.

How people on GLP-1s actually hit it

  • Protein first, every meal. With a small appetite, the order matters: eat the protein before the rest, because the rest will not get eaten.
  • Dense sources. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, eggs, fish, poultry, lean meat, tofu and tempeh deliver the most protein per mouthful. Liquid protein (milk, a protein shake) is easier on days when nausea or early fullness make solid food hard.
  • Spread it. Three or four protein-containing meals or snacks across the day beat one large one, because muscle protein synthesis responds per meal.
  • Count for a week. Most people have no idea what they eat; a week of tracking usually shows the gap is bigger than they thought.

Our guide to what to eat on GLP-1 medication goes through meal structure when appetite is low, and the side-effects guide covers the nausea that often stands between people and their protein.

sections.heading: Does resistance training prevent muscle loss on GLP-1 drugs?
sections.body:
Protein supplies the material; resistance training supplies the reason. In a calorie deficit the body is looking for tissue to shed, and unloaded muscle is a candidate. Loaded muscle is not. This is the oldest finding in the weight-loss literature and it has not changed with the drugs: people who lift during weight loss keep more lean mass than people who only walk, and people who walk keep more than people who do neither.

What "enough" looks like

Two sessions a week, each covering the major muscle groups (legs, hips, back, chest, shoulders, arms) with a resistance that makes the last two or three repetitions of a set hard, is the floor that most public-health and strength guidance converges on. It does not need a gym: bodyweight squats, push-ups against a counter, resistance bands and a pair of dumbbells cover it. It does need progression, meaning the resistance or the repetitions go up over the weeks, because muscle adapts to a load and then stops responding to it.

Why cardio alone is not enough

Walking, cycling and swimming are good for the heart, the mood and the appetite, and people on GLP-1 treatment should do them. They do not send a strong enough signal to preserve muscle in a deficit, and in large volumes they can add to the deficit and make the protein target harder to meet. The combination that works is modest cardio plus two resistance sessions, not a great deal of either. Our guide to exercise on GLP-1 medication covers starting points for people who have not trained before and the practicalities of training on an injection day.

The tiredness problem

A real obstacle is that people on these drugs often feel flat, particularly in the first weeks at a new dose, and training when under-fed and nauseated is unappealing. Two adjustments help: train on the days furthest from the injection, when side effects are usually lowest, and eat a protein-containing meal within a couple of hours of the session so the body has something to build with.

sections.heading: Bimagrumab and the muscle-sparing drugs: what BELIEVE showed
sections.body:
The pharmaceutical answer to the muscle question is a class of drugs that block the signals telling muscle to shrink, and the furthest along is bimagrumab, an antibody against the activin type II receptor. In the BELIEVE phase 2b trial, presented at the American Diabetes Association meeting in June 2025 and reported widely, 507 adults with obesity received semaglutide, bimagrumab or both over 72 weeks. As reported, the combination produced about 22% weight loss against about 16% for semaglutide alone, and about 93% of the weight lost on the combination was fat, compared with about 72% on semaglutide alone. On bimagrumab alone, lean mass went up while fat went down. Sources: Healio, June 23, 2025; EurekAlert, 2025, checked October 28, 2026.

Three cautions keep this in proportion. It is a phase 2 trial, presented at a conference and reported by the trade press; the full publication followed later and the figures above are as reported, not verified against the primary paper by us. Bimagrumab was given by intravenous infusion every twelve weeks in this trial, which is not how anyone buys a weight-loss drug. And the bimagrumab groups reported side effects, including acne and muscle spasms, that the researchers said need more study. It is not approved, it is not for sale, and anything sold online under that name or a similar one is not the trial drug.

Why it matters anyway

BELIEVE is the proof that the lean-loss problem is tractable and that the next generation of weight-loss treatment will be judged on body composition, not on the scale alone. Several companies are running similar programmes. For a reader deciding what to do in 2026, the conclusion is simpler: the drugs that spare muscle are years away, and the methods that spare muscle are available today for the cost of groceries and a set of dumbbells.

sections.heading: Who is this not for, and what are the limits of the evidence?
sections.body:
This guide is for adults on, or considering, a prescribed GLP-1 weight-loss medication who want to keep the muscle they have. It is not for:

  • Anyone thinking of lowering, spacing or splitting a dose to protect muscle. The trials that produced the lean-mass figures used the labelled doses, and the protective tools work at those doses. Dosing outside the label is a prescriber's decision and is covered, with the evidence, in our microdosing guide.
  • People with kidney disease or other conditions that limit protein, for whom a higher protein intake needs a clinician's sign-off first.
  • Adults over about 70 or anyone with existing sarcopenia, who should be losing weight under supervision with function measured, not on a telehealth subscription alone.
  • Anyone looking for a supplement answer. No supplement has evidence for preventing lean loss on GLP-1 treatment beyond ordinary protein, and products marketed for "GLP-1 muscle protection" are marketing.

The limits of what is known are real. DXA cannot separate muscle from water and support tissue; the substudies were small; the trials did not measure strength, with the exception of the small SEMALEAN cohort; and no trial has yet tested a protein-and-training programme against usual care in people on these drugs, which is the study that would settle the question. Until it exists, the advice rests on decades of weight-loss physiology rather than on GLP-1-specific trials, and this guide says so.

sections.heading: Final verdict and next steps
sections.body:
The muscle objection to GLP-1 treatment is half right. Lean mass does fall, by roughly a quarter to two-fifths of the weight lost in the scanned trials, and part of that is muscle. It is also what happens with any large weight loss, function was maintained where it was measured, and the two things that protect muscle cost almost nothing. A person who eats protein first at every meal, lifts twice a week and loses weight at the rate the label produces will end up lighter and, in most cases, stronger relative to their size.

  1. This week: track protein for seven days and find the gap. Add one resistance session, even if it is bands in the kitchen.
  2. At the next check-in: ask the prescriber or a dietitian for a protein target that fits your kidneys, age and weight, and mention any dizziness, weakness or falls.
  3. Choosing a provider: ask who will talk to you about nutrition and training. Our provider guide covers the rest of the checks, and the cost calculator totals the verified prices.
  4. If you are over 60 or already low on muscle: lose weight under supervision, with grip strength or a sit-to-stand test tracked alongside the scale.

References and further reading

  • Wilding JPH et al. Once-weekly semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity (STEP 1). NEJM, 2021, including the DXA substudy.
  • Jastreboff AM et al. Tirzepatide once weekly for the treatment of obesity (SURMOUNT-1). NEJM, 2022, including the body-composition substudy.
  • Healio: Combination bimagrumab plus semaglutide confers weight loss while preserving lean mass (BELIEVE, ADA 2025) and EurekAlert release.
  • SEMALEAN: impact of semaglutide on fat mass, lean mass and muscle function, 2025.
  • Barbell Medicine: GLP-1 muscle loss evidence review, 2026.
  • National Academies: Dietary Reference Intakes for protein.
  • Wegovy prescribing information, FDA for the labelled dose schedule.

This article is general information, not medical advice. Do not change a prescribed dose, start a new exercise programme after a long break, or raise protein intake with kidney disease without a licensed clinician who knows your history.

articles.title: Next-Generation Weight Loss Drugs (2026): What's Coming
articles.description: Retatrutide, CagriSema, amycretin, MariTide, survodutide and the amylin drugs: trial results, phases, company timelines and what they mean for you.
articles.author: Treatments Hub Research Team
keyTakeaways: Two candidates are closest to US pharmacies. Novo Nordisk filed CagriSema with the FDA on December 18, 2025 and expects a decision in the fourth quarter of 2026; Lilly says it will file retatrutide in the first quarter of 2027. Both dates are company statements, not approvals.

Retatrutide has the largest published phase 3 result: 25.0% average weight loss at 80 weeks on the top dose in TRIUMPH-1, counting everyone randomised, against 3.9% on placebo (NEJM, September 2026). Lilly's own on-treatment figure is 28.3%.

Amylin is the next mechanism. CagriSema, amycretin, petrelintide and eloralintide all add or use amylin signalling, but in the only completed phase 3 head-to-head so far (REDEFINE 4) CagriSema produced less weight loss than tirzepatide 15 mg, 20.2% versus 23.6%.

None of the pipeline drugs can be legally compounded, and the FDA has warned sellers of "research use" retatrutide. If you need treatment now, the approved drugs work now; a prescriber can move you to a new one later if it is approved and suits you.

sections.heading: What are the next-generation weight-loss drugs, and when will they arrive?
sections.body:
The short answerThe next wave is led by retatrutide (Lilly, a triple GLP-1, GIP and glucagon agonist, 25.0% weight loss at 80 weeks in its main phase 3 trial) and CagriSema (Novo Nordisk, semaglutide plus the amylin analogue cagrilintide, 20.4% at 68 weeks). CagriSema is under FDA review with a decision the company expects in late 2026; Lilly says it will file retatrutide in early 2027. Amycretin, MariTide, survodutide and the amylin drugs are a step or more behind. None is approved in the US, and none can be legally compounded.

The weight-loss drugs most people know, semaglutide (Wegovy, Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Zepbound, Mounjaro), are no longer the newest thing on the shelf. Since December 2025 the FDA has approved a semaglutide pill, a small-molecule GLP-1 pill and a higher-dose semaglutide injection. Behind them sits a pipeline that is larger and further along than at any point before, and the October 2026 coverage reflects that: Time's October 1, 2026 report was titled "The Next Generation of Weight-Loss Drugs Is Almost Here", and Quartz, updating its tracker on October 28, 2026, named CagriSema, retatrutide and the oral drug aleniglipron as the three to watch, with only one of them filed with regulators.

This guide sets out each candidate we could source: what it does in the body, its best published or reported trial result and which kind of result that is, its trial phase, what the company has said about filing or launch, what it has shown on side effects, and what it might mean for someone already on semaglutide or tirzepatide. Where a company has announced a result that has not been peer-reviewed, we say so and give the date. Where two figures circulate for the same trial, we say why and which one is the like-for-like comparison.

A 36-week result in 125 people is not comparable with an 80-week result in 2,339. The sections below give each figure its context, and the section on what the numbers mean explains the two kinds of average that every company now reports.

sections.heading: What is already approved, and what is still in trials?
sections.body:
Three things changed for US patients between December 2025 and April 2026, and they matter because they are available now, not in two years. They also show what "next generation" looks like in practice: the first new options were not new mechanisms but new forms and doses of the existing ones.

Approved in the US

  • The Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide 25 mg, Novo Nordisk). Approved for chronic weight management in a release dated December 22, 2025, as the first oral GLP-1 cleared for that use, per Becker's Hospital Review. In its phase 3 trial, OASIS 4, weight fell by 13.6% at 64 weeks against 2.2% on placebo among 307 adults without diabetes (NEJM, 2025, via PubMed).
  • Foundayo (orforglipron, Eli Lilly). A small-molecule GLP-1 pill that can be taken without food or water rules. Quartz records its FDA approval earlier in 2026; our Foundayo vs Wegovy pill guide covers the April 1, 2026 approval, its 11.2% result at the top dose over 72 weeks in ATTAIN-1, and the prices Lilly publishes.
  • Wegovy HD (semaglutide 7.2 mg weekly). Approved on March 19, 2026 for adults with obesity who have been on the 2.4 mg dose for at least four weeks, per Novo Nordisk's release and Healio. It is a higher rung on the existing ladder, not a new drug.

Filed and under review

Only one new mechanism is at that stage in the US: CagriSema. Novo Nordisk announced its FDA submission on December 18, 2025, and coverage since, including Clinical Trials Arena, puts the expected decision in late 2026. As of October 31, 2026, we found no report of a decision.

In phase 3 or about to be

Retatrutide has finished its four core phase 3 trials and Lilly plans to file in early 2027. Amycretin, MariTide, eloralintide and aleniglipron are in phase 3. Survodutide has reported its first phase 3 obesity trials. Petrelintide is moving from phase 2 into phase 3. Bimagrumab is in phase 2. Each is covered below.

What the phases mean for you

StageWhat it meansCan a doctor prescribe it?Can a pharmacy legally compound it?
Phase 1 / phase 2Small and mid-sized trials testing safety and dose; results can change a lot laterNo, only within a trialNo
Phase 3Large trials, usually thousands of people, designed to support approvalNo, only within a trialNo
Filed (under FDA review)The company has asked for approval; the FDA can approve, ask for more data, or refuseNoNo
ApprovedThe FDA has approved a label: who it is for, at which doses, with which warningsYes, on prescriptionOnly in narrow circumstances that apply to approved drugs
Approved abroad onlyApproved by another regulator, such as China'sNot as a US prescriptionNo

The practical rule: until a drug reaches the bottom of that table in the US, the only legitimate way to take it is inside a registered clinical trial. A positive phase 3 result is good news about the future and changes nothing about what is available this month. A filing date is a company's plan, not a promise, and the retatrutide filing has already moved once, as the next sections show.

sections.heading: How should you read the weight-loss numbers in new drug headlines?
sections.body:
With three questions in mind: which kind of average is it, how long was the trial, and who was in it. Almost every confusing claim about the new drugs comes from mixing figures that answer different questions. This section explains the vocabulary once, so the rest of the guide can be read quickly.

Two averages from the same trial

Modern obesity trials report two main results, which regulators call estimands.

  • Everyone randomised (called treatment-policy or treatment-regimen). Every person who was assigned to the drug is counted, including people who stopped taking it, missed doses or started another treatment. This is the closer guide to what happens when a group of real people is prescribed the drug. Journals usually lead with it.
  • On treatment (called the efficacy or trial-product estimand). This estimates the result if everyone had kept taking the drug as directed. It describes what the drug can do in people who stay on it. Companies usually lead with it, because it is larger.

Neither number is dishonest. They answer different questions. The problem is only when one drug's on-treatment number is set against another drug's everyone-randomised number, which flatters the first. Retatrutide shows the gap clearly: Lilly's May 2026 release led with 28.3% on 12 mg, and the NEJM paper led with 25.0%. Same trial, same dose, same 80 weeks. In REDEFINE 4, as reported, tirzepatide's figures were 23.6% and 25.5%, and CagriSema's 20.2% and 23.0%.

Placebo-adjusted figures

Some companies report weight loss with the placebo group's result already subtracted. Structure Therapeutics' aleniglipron topline is an example: 11.3% placebo-adjusted. If the placebo group lost 2% to 3%, as is typical in these trials, the raw figure would be a few points higher. A placebo-adjusted number cannot be compared directly with a raw one.

Length and population

Weight loss on these drugs keeps falling for a year or more before it levels off, so a 36-week result is not comparable with an 80-week one. The MariTide researchers wrote that weight had not plateaued at 52 weeks (NEJM, 2025). Population matters as much: people with type 2 diabetes lose less on every drug in the class, which is why retatrutide produced 25.0% in TRIUMPH-1 and up to 20.8% in TRIUMPH-2, and CagriSema 20.4% in REDEFINE 1 but 13.7% in REDEFINE 2. Small early trials, like amycretin's 125-person study, also tend to recruit healthier volunteers at lower BMIs than phase 3.

Like-for-like: everyone-randomised results we could source

The table below lines up the everyone-randomised figures, so the comparisons are as fair as separate trials allow. It is still a cross-trial comparison, and the only true head-to-head in it is REDEFINE 4.

Sources are in each drug's section; the Wegovy HD, Wegovy 2.4 mg and Foundayo rows follow our dosing evidence guide and Foundayo guide. Eloralintide and amycretin are left out because we have only on-treatment or early-phase figures for them.

A worked example in pounds

Averages in percent are easy to over-read, so here is the arithmetic for one person starting at 250 pounds, using the everyone-randomised figures. Retatrutide's 25.0% would be about 62 pounds; tirzepatide's 23.6% in REDEFINE 4 about 59; CagriSema's 20.4% in REDEFINE 1 about 51; Wegovy HD's 18.7% about 47; the Wegovy pill's 13.6% about 34. The gap between the strongest approved drug and the strongest pipeline drug, on these numbers, is a few pounds on average, not dozens. The gap between any of them and the placebo arms, which lost 2% to 4%, is far larger. Individual results spread widely around every one of these averages, and some people on each drug lose little.

A checklist for any new-drug headline

  1. Is the figure everyone randomised or on treatment?
  2. Is it raw or placebo-adjusted?
  3. How many weeks, and was weight still falling?
  4. Did the trial include people with diabetes?
  5. Is it a press release, a conference presentation or a peer-reviewed paper?
  6. How many people stopped because of side effects?
  7. Was there a head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide, or only placebo?

A headline that cannot answer most of those is a headline, not evidence.

sections.heading: How much weight loss did retatrutide show in the TRIUMPH trials?
sections.body:
More than any obesity drug has shown in a phase 3 trial so far. Retatrutide is a once-weekly injection that Lilly describes as a triple hormone receptor agonist: it acts on the GLP-1 receptor (like semaglutide), the GIP receptor (like tirzepatide) and the glucagon receptor. Our retatrutide explainer covers the 2023 phase 2 trial, in which the top dose produced about 24% weight loss over 48 weeks. The TRIUMPH phase 3 programme has now reported four trials.

TRIUMPH-1: obesity without diabetes

The main trial randomised 2,339 adults with obesity or overweight to retatrutide 4 mg, 9 mg or 12 mg, or placebo, for 80 weeks. Lilly's topline release of May 21, 2026 reported average weight loss of 19.0%, 25.9% and 28.3% on the three doses, and said 45.3% of people on 12 mg lost 30% or more of their body weight. Those are the company's figures from its efficacy estimand, which describes people who stayed on the drug. Experts quoted by the Science Media Centre at the time stressed that this was an announcement, not a published study.

The full paper followed in the New England Journal of Medicine on September 29, 2026. Its abstract reports the treatment-regimen result, which counts everyone randomised whether or not they kept taking the drug: 25.0% average weight loss at 80 weeks on the 12 mg dose against 3.9% on placebo. That is the number to compare with other drugs' intention-to-treat results. The paper also reported less knee pain in the participants with knee osteoarthritis and fewer breathing interruptions in those with obstructive sleep apnoea; coverage of the abstract put those subgroups at 574 and 243 people. Lilly's June 6, 2026 release gave further detail on the knee, sleep apnoea and blood-sugar results.

TRIUMPH-4: obesity with knee osteoarthritis

This was the first phase 3 readout, in December 2025. BioPharma Dive reported average weight loss of 28.7% at 68 weeks on the highest dose, about 71 pounds, against 2.1% on placebo, alongside large reductions in knee pain. It was also where a new side effect drew attention: BioSpace reported dysesthesia, an altered or unpleasant skin sensation, in 8.8% of people on 9 mg and 20.9% on 12 mg against 0.7% on placebo.

TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3: diabetes and heart disease

Lilly announced both on July 23, 2026. In TRIUMPH-2, adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes lost up to 20.8% of body weight at 80 weeks on 12 mg, as reported by Drug Discovery World. In TRIUMPH-3, adults with severe obesity and established cardiovascular disease averaged 22.6% weight loss at 80 weeks on 12 mg. As with every obesity drug, weight loss was smaller in people with diabetes than without.

TrialPopulationLengthTop-dose resultType of figureStatus
TRIUMPH-1Obesity or overweight, no diabetes (2,339)80 weeks25.0% vs 3.9% placeboEveryone randomisedPublished, NEJM, Sept 2026
TRIUMPH-1Same80 weeks28.3% vs 2.2% placeboOn treatmentCompany release, May 2026
TRIUMPH-4Obesity with knee osteoarthritis68 weeks28.7% vs 2.1% placeboAs reportedCompany topline, Dec 2025
TRIUMPH-2Obesity with type 2 diabetes80 weeksUp to 20.8%As reportedCompany topline, July 2026
TRIUMPH-3Severe obesity with cardiovascular disease80 weeks22.6%As reportedCompany topline, July 2026

How it compares with tirzepatide

Not directly, yet. No published trial has put retatrutide against tirzepatide. The nearest benchmark is a recent head-to-head in which tirzepatide 15 mg was the comparator: in REDEFINE 4, tirzepatide produced 23.6% weight loss at 84 weeks counting everyone randomised. Retatrutide's 25.0% at 80 weeks in a different trial, with a different population, is close enough to that figure that the honest summary is "probably more, by an amount nobody has measured". Our tirzepatide vs semaglutide guide sets out the approved drugs' own trial numbers.

Side effects

Lilly's TRIUMPH-1 release gave the rate of people who stopped because of adverse events: 4.1% on 4 mg, 6.9% on 9 mg and 11.3% on 12 mg, against 4.9% on placebo. The NEJM paper reported gastrointestinal events as more frequent on retatrutide, the familiar pattern for the class. The dysesthesia signal from TRIUMPH-4 is the one genuinely new item, and it is dose-related. We did not find a published figure for how many people stopped treatment because of it.

What it might mean for people on semaglutide or tirzepatide

If retatrutide is approved on these results, the people most likely to be offered it first are those for whom the approved drugs have run out of road: people on tirzepatide 15 mg who have plateaued well short of their goal, and people with severe obesity where the gap between a 20% and a 25% average loss is clinically meaningful. Lilly's planned filing also covers knee osteoarthritis pain and obstructive sleep apnoea, which could matter for coverage if insurers treat those conditions differently from weight alone. For someone doing well on semaglutide or tirzepatide, the trial results are not a reason to switch. A larger average comes with a higher rate of stopping at the top dose and a new side effect, and the right comparison is not retatrutide against nothing but retatrutide against the drug you already tolerate. That comparison will be clearer once the label, and ideally a head-to-head result, exist.

When could retatrutide be approved?

Not before 2027, on Lilly's own timeline. On July 23, 2026, alongside the TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 results, Lilly said it plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the FDA in the first quarter of 2027, for obesity, knee osteoarthritis pain and obstructive sleep apnoea, as reported by RTTNews and Drug Discovery World. Lilly had previously aimed for 2026; it said the extra time was to complete the chemistry, manufacturing and controls package that a biologic application requires, not because of the clinical results.

What happens after filing

After a filing, the FDA reviews the application, inspects manufacturing and decides. Standard reviews usually take most of a year. In 2026 the agency approved two obesity products much faster under its national priority voucher programme: our Foundayo guide records Foundayo's approval 50 days after filing, and Novo Nordisk said Wegovy HD went through the same programme. Whether retatrutide receives a voucher is not something Lilly has announced in the sources we found. Our own reading, not a company statement: a first-quarter 2027 filing points to a decision somewhere between mid-2027, if a voucher applies, and 2028, on a standard review.

What could change the timing

  • Manufacturing. The delay already announced was about the manufacturing data package. That is the part of the application outside the trials.
  • Safety review. The FDA will look closely at dysesthesia, heart rate and anything else that differs from the GLP-1 class, and can ask for more data.
  • The cardiovascular question. TRIUMPH-3 enrolled people with heart disease and reported weight loss; Lilly said it will present the cardiovascular data at future meetings. The label at launch will reflect whatever the FDA accepts from it.

Until approval, retatrutide is investigational. Lilly is not selling it, no US doctor can prescribe it outside a trial, and no pharmacy can legally compound it. The next section covers what is being sold online under its name.

sections.heading: Is "research peptide" retatrutide sold online safe or legal?
sections.body:
No to both, on the FDA's stated position. Retatrutide is widely sold online as a "research peptide", often as a powder in a vial with a label saying "for research use only" or "not for human consumption". These products are not Lilly's drug, have not been approved, and have not been tested for what is actually in the vial.

What the FDA says

The FDA's page on unapproved GLP-1 drugs used for weight loss states that retatrutide and cagrilintide (the amylin half of CagriSema) cannot be used in compounding under federal law, because they are not components of an FDA-approved drug and have not been found safe and effective for any condition. The same page says the agency has warned companies selling semaglutide, tirzepatide or retatrutide falsely labelled "for research purposes" or "not for human consumption", has warned telehealth firms marketing retatrutide, and has issued warning letters to distributors of the active ingredient. The "research use" label does not make a product legal to sell for people to inject.

Drugs.com's explainer summarises the consumer position plainly: products sold as "retatrutide", "retatrutide peptide" or "reta" are not FDA-approved, are not legal to sell for human use, and are not tested for safety, purity or correct dose. Lilly has also gone to court: HMP Global Learning Network reported that the company has filed lawsuits over alleged sales of unapproved retatrutide.

Why this matters more than the legal point

  • You do not know what is in the vial. The trial results describe Lilly's manufactured product at known doses. A grey-market powder may contain a different amount, a different peptide, impurities, or nothing.
  • The dose in the trials was escalated under supervision. The phase 3 participants were stepped up over weeks with monitoring. A reconstituted powder has no label, no titration and no clinician watching for the side effects that made some trial participants stop.
  • The new side effect is not well understood yet. Dysesthesia was dose-related in the trials. Nobody is tracking it in people injecting unlabelled product.
  • There is no recourse. If something goes wrong, there is no pharmacist, no prescriber and no manufacturer accountable for the product.

The same applies to anything sold online as cagrilintide, CagriSema, amycretin, survodutide or any other pipeline name. If a website offers a drug that is in phase 3, it is not offering the drug from the phase 3 trial. We do not describe sources, doses or reconstitution for any of these products and never will. Our compounded vs brand-name guide explains how legitimate compounding of approved drugs differs.

sections.heading: What did CagriSema show, and when will the FDA decide?
sections.body:
CagriSema is a once-weekly injection that combines two drugs: semaglutide 2.4 mg, the active ingredient of Wegovy, and cagrilintide 2.4 mg, a long-acting analogue of the hormone amylin. Novo Nordisk's filing release describes it as the first once-weekly combination of GLP-1 and amylin analogues for weight management. It is the closest new mechanism to US approval.

REDEFINE 1: obesity without diabetes

The main trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in June 2025 (Garvey et al., NEJM, 2025), randomised 3,417 adults with obesity or overweight to CagriSema, semaglutide alone, cagrilintide alone or placebo for 68 weeks. Counting everyone randomised, weight fell by 20.4% on CagriSema against 3.0% on placebo, as summarised by the American College of Cardiology's journal scan. The figure often quoted in the press, about 23%, as in Scientific American's coverage, is the on-treatment figure for people who kept taking it. The trial also showed that each component alone did less than the two together, which is the point of a combination.

REDEFINE 2: obesity with type 2 diabetes

In 1,206 adults with type 2 diabetes (Davies et al., NEJM, 2025), weight fell by 13.7% at 68 weeks against 3.4% on placebo, per the ACC summary. Gastrointestinal side effects were reported in about 80% of people on CagriSema against about 40% on placebo.

REDEFINE 4: the head-to-head with tirzepatide

This is the result that changed how CagriSema is discussed. Novo Nordisk announced on February 23, 2026 that the open-label trial in 809 adults had not met its primary endpoint: CagriSema did not show non-inferiority to tirzepatide 15 mg on weight loss at 84 weeks. Counting everyone randomised, weight fell by 20.2% on CagriSema and 23.6% on tirzepatide; on treatment, 23.0% and 25.5%, as reported by Drug Topics. In other words, the newest combination from Novo produced less weight loss than the best drug already on the market.

Filing and what comes next

The December 18, 2025 filing covers CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition. Novo's guidance, as reported by Clinical Trials Arena, points to a decision in late 2026. Novo's February 2026 company announcement filed with the SEC also describes a phase 3 trial, REDEFINE 11, exploring the full weight-loss potential of the 2.4/2.4 mg dose, with data expected in the first half of 2027, and a higher-dose phase 3 trial planned to start in the second half of 2026. Those are company plans.

What Time added

Time's October 2026 report used CagriSema as the lead example of the amylin approach, and reported that in people with type 2 diabetes the drug reduced harmful fat in the liver and pancreas, an early sign of benefits beyond the scale. It also reported a figure every reader of this guide should hold onto: roughly 40% of people who start these drugs stop within a year, mostly because of gastrointestinal side effects. A drug that is easier to stay on can beat a stronger drug that people stop.

What it might mean for people on semaglutide

CagriSema contains the same semaglutide dose as Wegovy, with cagrilintide added. If it is approved, the obvious candidates are people on Wegovy who have plateaued at 2.4 mg and want more effect from a product built on the drug they already tolerate. They will also have Wegovy HD, which is already approved, and tirzepatide, which beat CagriSema in REDEFINE 4. Which of those three a prescriber picks will depend on the label, coverage and how the person handled semaglutide.

For people on tirzepatide, CagriSema is harder to argue for on the evidence so far. REDEFINE 4 tested exactly that comparison, against tirzepatide's top dose, and CagriSema came out behind on both estimands. Someone doing well on tirzepatide has no trial-based reason to move to it. The more relevant amylin development for that group is Lilly's EloraTZP, which adds amylin to tirzepatide rather than replacing it, covered below. If the FDA approves CagriSema in late 2026, our Zepbound vs Wegovy guide and this page will be updated with its label, its doses and what the companies say about price.

sections.heading: Why is amylin the next mechanism?
sections.body:
Because it works on appetite through a different hormone system, which opens two possibilities: more weight loss when combined with a GLP-1, and possibly a gentler experience when used alone. Amylin is a hormone released by the pancreas alongside insulin after meals. It signals fullness and slows how fast the stomach empties. Drug versions of it last much longer than the natural hormone, and the pipeline now contains four distinct ways of using it.

  • Combination of two drugs: CagriSema, cagrilintide plus semaglutide in one weekly injection.
  • One molecule that does both: amycretin, a single molecule designed to act on the GLP-1 and amylin receptors.
  • Amylin alone: petrelintide (Zealand and Roche) and eloralintide (Lilly), tested as stand-alone weight-loss drugs.
  • Amylin added to tirzepatide: Lilly's EloraTZP, eloralintide combined with tirzepatide.

The case for amylin

The argument made by the companies, and reflected in Time's coverage, is that the next big gain may not come from more weight loss but from weight loss that is easier to tolerate and keep. If the stand-alone amylin drugs can produce meaningful weight loss with less nausea than GLP-1s, they could suit the many people who stop GLP-1 treatment because of side effects. Roche described petrelintide's tolerability as comparable to placebo in its March 2026 phase 2 release. The other argument is additive: in REDEFINE 1 the combination beat both of its components on their own.

The case for caution

Amylin drugs have not yet proved they beat the best existing drug. CagriSema lost to tirzepatide in its head-to-head trial. Petrelintide's phase 2 result, up to about 10.7%, divided analysts, as Clinical Trials Arena reported: one argued the modest size could limit real-world use, while another said the data supported a well-tolerated base for combinations. And amylin combinations still cause gastrointestinal effects; in REDEFINE 2, about 80% of people on CagriSema reported them.

Mechanism comparison

sections.heading: Amycretin: Novo's single-molecule amylin and GLP-1 drug
sections.body:
Amycretin is Novo Nordisk's attempt to put both signals into one molecule rather than two drugs in one pen. It is being developed as a weekly injection and as a daily pill, which makes it one of the few pipeline drugs aiming for both forms.

The early result that drew attention

In a phase 1b/2a trial published in The Lancet in June 2025, 125 adults with a BMI of 25 to 34.9 were randomised to injected amycretin or placebo at a single site in San Antonio. The estimated mean weight loss was 24.3% at 36 weeks on the 60 mg dose and 22.0% on 20 mg, against about 1% on placebo, as summarised by the American College of Cardiology. The most common side effects were mild to moderate gastrointestinal events that rose with dose.

That number is often set next to retatrutide's, and it should not be. The trial was small, short, run at one site, in people with lower BMIs than the phase 3 obesity trials, and designed mainly to test safety and dose. Early-phase results in obesity have tended to shrink when tested in larger, longer, more varied populations. It is a reason to run phase 3, not a forecast of the phase 3 result.

Diabetes results

In people with type 2 diabetes, Novo reported in November 2025 that injected amycretin produced up to 14.5% weight loss over 36 weeks against 2.6% on placebo, per CNBC, and Pharmaphorum reported up to 10.1% with the oral form. Novo said it would take both forms into phase 3 in diabetes.

Phase 3 status and timing

Novo announced on June 12, 2025 that it would advance both injected and oral amycretin into phase 3 for weight management, starting in the first quarter of 2026, after end-of-phase 2 discussions with regulators. Novo's 2026 quarterly filings describe 84-week phase 3 obesity trials named AMAZE 1 and AMAZE 2 of a once-weekly injection under the name zenagamtide; trade coverage identifies that as amycretin's new name, which we could not confirm from a Novo statement, so treat the naming as reported. No filing date has been stated. An 84-week trial that began in 2026 cannot read out before 2027 at the earliest, so a US approval before 2028 would require a timeline no company has announced.

What it might mean for you

Nothing for treatment decisions in 2026 or 2027. If you are on semaglutide now, the more relevant Novo products in the next year are Wegovy HD and, if approved, CagriSema.

sections.heading: Petrelintide and eloralintide: can amylin work on its own?
sections.body:
Two companies are testing whether amylin alone can be a weight-loss drug, without a GLP-1 attached. If it can, it would give people who cannot tolerate GLP-1s an option, and give prescribers a building block for combinations.

Petrelintide (Zealand Pharma and Roche)

Roche announced the phase 2 ZUPREME-1 results on March 5, 2026: in 493 adults with overweight or obesity, petrelintide produced up to 10.7% mean weight loss at 42 weeks against 1.7% on placebo. Roche described tolerability as comparable to placebo, and withdrawal from the trial for any reason was 8.4% across the petrelintide arms against 13.6% on placebo. Zealand later announced publication in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, where the treatment-policy figure was up to 10.2% against 1.4%. The two companies have said they will move it into phase 3, per BioPharm International; reports differ on the exact start date.

The honest summary is that petrelintide's weight loss is about what older GLP-1 doses produced, with the gut side effects looking milder in phase 2. Whether that trade appeals depends on the person. Analysts were split on whether the market wants it.

Eloralintide (Eli Lilly)

Lilly's amylin agonist had the stronger stand-alone phase 2. Lilly's November 6, 2025 release, issued as the trial was presented at ObesityWeek and published in The Lancet, reported up to 20.1% mean weight loss at 48 weeks on the 9 mg dose against 0.4% on placebo in 263 adults, using the efficacy estimand. The main side effects were mild to moderate gastrointestinal symptoms and fatigue, greater at higher doses. Lilly has registered phase 3 trials, including a study in obesity without type 2 diabetes.

EloraTZP: amylin added to tirzepatide

The combination result is newer. Lilly's September 30, 2026 release reported a 48-week phase 2b trial in 367 adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes. The top combination, eloralintide 9 mg plus tirzepatide 15 mg, produced up to 23.3% weight loss against 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg alone and 3.0% on placebo, with a larger fall in A1C. The cost was tolerability: discontinuation ranged from 10.8% to 27.0% across the combination arms, against 2.9% on tirzepatide alone. Lilly says it plans to start phase 3 of the combination by the end of 2026. These are company-reported results from a conference presentation, not a peer-reviewed paper.

That 23.3% in people with diabetes is notable, because weight loss in diabetes trials normally runs well below non-diabetes trials. It is the first evidence that adding amylin to tirzepatide does what CagriSema did for semaglutide. It is also a phase 2 trial with high dropout in some arms.

sections.heading: Could MariTide replace weekly injections with a monthly shot?
sections.body:
That is Amgen's aim. Maridebart cafraglutide, branded in development as MariTide, combines an antibody with GLP-1-activating peptides. As Drugs.com's explainer sets out, it activates the GLP-1 receptor and blocks the GIP receptor, the opposite of what tirzepatide does at GIP. That both approaches produce weight loss is one of the open scientific puzzles of the field. The practical point is the dosing interval: MariTide was tested once a month or less often, rather than weekly.

The phase 2 result

The phase 2 trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2025 (Jastreboff et al., NEJM, 2025), randomised 592 adults across an obesity cohort and an obesity-with-diabetes cohort. In the obesity cohort, counting everyone randomised, mean weight loss at 52 weeks ranged from 12.3% to 16.2% across dose regimens against 2.5% on placebo; the on-treatment figure reached about 19.9%. In the diabetes cohort, weight loss ranged from 8.4% to 12.3% against 1.7%. The researchers wrote that weight had not plateaued at 52 weeks, so longer trials are needed to see the full effect.

Phase 3

Amgen's MARITIME phase 3 programme is under way. Amgen's own account of the drug was published in May 2026. The registry lists, among others, MARITIME-SWITCH, which enrols adults moving from a weekly GLP-1 to MariTide, and long-term extensions such as the MARITIME-1 extension, with estimated primary completion in late 2027. We found no Amgen statement of a filing date.

What it might mean for people on semaglutide or tirzepatide

MariTide is the pipeline drug most explicitly designed for people already on treatment: the existence of a switch trial says so. If it reaches the market, its pitch will be fewer injections rather than more weight loss, and the phase 2 numbers put it in the range of the approved weekly drugs rather than above them. For anyone who dislikes weekly injections, the realistic options before MariTide could be approved are the two approved pills, compared in our pills vs injections guide.

sections.heading: Survodutide and the glucagon drugs: what does the liver data add?
sections.body:
Survodutide, from Boehringer Ingelheim, is a weekly injection that acts on the glucagon and GLP-1 receptors. Glucagon is the hormone that normally raises blood sugar between meals; activating its receptor in this way is intended to increase energy use and pull fat out of the liver. Retatrutide also has a glucagon arm. Survodutide is the first glucagon-GLP-1 drug to report phase 3 obesity results.

SYNCHRONIZE-1

Boehringer announced positive data from two phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE obesity trials in 2026, and the full SYNCHRONIZE-1 results were presented at the American Diabetes Association meeting in June 2026 and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Per the American College of Cardiology's journal scan, counting everyone randomised, mean weight change at 76 weeks was 12.2% on 3.6 mg and 13.0% on 6.0 mg against 5.4% on placebo. The company's on-treatment figure was up to 16.6% against 3.2%.

Liver and visceral fat

Boehringer's emphasis is where the fat comes from. In a pre-specified substudy reported by the company, survodutide reduced visceral fat by up to 34% and liver fat by up to 63.1%; the SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD results were published in Nature Medicine. That fits the liver indication Boehringer is also pursuing, in people with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease.

The tolerability problem

The weakness is how many people stopped. Fierce Biotech's reading of the NEJM paper put discontinuation due to adverse events at nearly 24% on 3.6 mg and nearly 25% on 6 mg, against about 5.4% on placebo, with discontinuations concentrated during dose escalation. Boehringer described the safety profile as broadly consistent with the GLP-1 class. For comparison, retatrutide's top dose had 11.3% stopping for adverse events in TRIUMPH-1, and the Wegovy pill about 7% in OASIS 4.

What it might mean for you

On weight alone, survodutide's phase 3 result sits below tirzepatide and around semaglutide. Its case rests on the liver. For someone with fatty liver disease, it may become relevant if Boehringer files and the FDA approves; we found no stated filing date. For most people choosing a weight-loss drug, it does not change the decision.

sections.heading: What changed with Wegovy HD and the new pills?
sections.body:
The most immediate "next generation" for patients is not a new mechanism. It is more choice within the two mechanisms already approved, and three of those choices arrived in five months.

Wegovy HD: semaglutide 7.2 mg

Novo Nordisk announced FDA approval on March 19, 2026. Wegovy HD is a weekly 7.2 mg semaglutide injection for adults with obesity who have taken the 2.4 mg dose for at least four weeks and need more weight reduction, per Healio. It was approved on the STEP UP trial, in which the company reports 20.7% average weight loss at 72 weeks among people who stayed on 7.2 mg. Counting everyone randomised, the published figures were 18.7% on 7.2 mg, 15.6% on 2.4 mg and 3.9% on placebo, as set out in our GLP-1 dosing evidence guide. Side effects were mostly gastrointestinal and rose at the higher dose, and the FDA noted more skin sensation problems, the same dysesthesia signal seen with retatrutide, which generally resolved on their own or with a lower dose (Healio).

What it means: for someone on Wegovy 2.4 mg who tolerates it and has stalled, there is now an approved step up within the same drug. It is a prescriber's decision, under the label, and it is available now.

The Wegovy pill: oral semaglutide 25 mg

Approved in December 2025 (Becker's), the Wegovy pill produced 13.6% weight loss at 64 weeks against 2.2% on placebo in OASIS 4, with 30% of people losing at least 20% of body weight (ACC journal scan). Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 74.0% against 42.2% on placebo (NEJM via PubMed). It must be taken on an empty stomach with a sip of water and a 30-minute wait before eating.

Foundayo: orforglipron

Foundayo is Lilly's small-molecule GLP-1 pill, approved on April 1, 2026, which can be taken at any time with or without food. Our Foundayo vs Wegovy pill guide covers its 11.2% top-dose result in ATTAIN-1, the ATTAIN-MAINTAIN switch data, and the self-pay and insurance prices. It matters for this guide for one reason: it is the template the pipeline pills are chasing.

Aleniglipron and the next oral drugs

Structure Therapeutics' aleniglipron is a once-daily small-molecule GLP-1 pill, the same kind of drug as Foundayo. The company's December 8, 2025 topline reported a placebo-adjusted mean weight loss of 11.3% at 36 weeks on 120 mg in the ACCESS phase 2b trial, and up to 15.3% placebo-adjusted on 240 mg in the exploratory ACCESS II study. Discontinuation due to adverse events ranged from 7.7% to 13.3% across doses. In its second-quarter 2026 results, Structure said it had dosed the first patients in the ACCOMPLISH phase 3 programme. No filing date has been stated. "Placebo-adjusted" means the placebo group's loss has already been subtracted, so these figures are not directly comparable with Foundayo's or the Wegovy pill's unadjusted ones.

Ecnoglutide: approved outside the US

Not every new weight-loss drug is following a US path first. Ecnoglutide, from Sciwind Biosciences, is a weekly GLP-1 injection that China's drug regulator approved for chronic weight management in March 2026. Sciwind describes it as the first approved cAMP-biased GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight management, meaning it is designed to favour one of the receptor's internal signalling routes. The approval rests on the SLIMMER phase 3 trial in Chinese adults, published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology in 2025, in which participants on the highest dose lost a mean 15.4% at 48 weeks, as reported. Pfizer holds commercial rights in mainland China under a February 2026 deal.

For US readers, the practical point is short. Ecnoglutide is not approved by the FDA, we found no US trial programme for it, and it cannot be legally prescribed or compounded here. Its result in Chinese adults sits in the range of semaglutide. It is in this guide because it appears in search results as a "new weight-loss drug", and because it shows how many GLP-1 drugs are now being developed worldwide: the mechanism is no longer one or two companies' property.

sections.heading: Will bimagrumab and other muscle-sparing drugs protect lean mass?
sections.body:
They are the most interesting answer to the most common objection to GLP-1 treatment, and they are the furthest from pharmacies. Our GLP-1 muscle loss guide covers what the semaglutide and tirzepatide body-composition substudies showed and what protects muscle today. The short version: lean mass made up roughly a quarter to two-fifths of the weight lost in those substudies, and protein plus resistance training are the tools that work now.

What BELIEVE showed

Bimagrumab is an antibody that blocks the activin type II receptors, signals that tell muscle to shrink. In the BELIEVE phase 2 trial, now published in Nature Medicine, adults with obesity received semaglutide, bimagrumab or both for 72 weeks. The high-dose combination produced 22.1% weight loss (24.2 kg) against 15.7% on semaglutide 2.4 mg alone and 10.8% on bimagrumab alone. As our muscle guide reports from the conference presentation, about 93% of the weight lost on the combination was fat.

Why it is still years away

  • It is phase 2. No phase 3 trial of bimagrumab for obesity was reported in the sources we found.
  • It was given by intravenous infusion in BELIEVE, which is not how anyone expects to take a weight-loss drug.
  • The tirzepatide programme has narrowed. Clinical Trials Arena reported that Lilly terminated a phase 2b study of tirzepatide plus bimagrumab in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes in September 2025, while a study in obesity alone continued.

What it means for you: nothing for the next few years except that the industry now judges weight-loss drugs on body composition, not just the scale. Anything sold online as bimagrumab is not the trial drug. The muscle you keep in 2026 depends on what you eat and lift.

sections.heading: How do the side effects of the new drugs compare?
sections.body:
None of the pipeline drugs escapes the GLP-1 pattern. Where a drug acts on the GLP-1 receptor, the gut effects come with it: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation, worst during dose increases, usually easing with time. The differences are in how often, how many people stop, and whether anything new appears. The table brings together the figures we could source, with their trial, so you can see which comparisons are fair.

Drug (trial)Gastrointestinal eventsStopped due to adverse eventsOther signal reported
Retatrutide (TRIUMPH-1)More frequent than placebo (NEJM)4.1% / 6.9% / 11.3% on 4 / 9 / 12 mg vs 4.9% placebo (Lilly)Dysesthesia 8.8% / 20.9% on 9 / 12 mg vs 0.7% (TRIUMPH-4, BioSpace)
CagriSema (REDEFINE 2)About 80% vs 40% placebo (ACC summary)Not sourced hereDid not match tirzepatide's weight loss (REDEFINE 4)
Survodutide (SYNCHRONIZE-1)Main reason for stoppingNearly 24% / 25% on 3.6 / 6 mg vs about 5.4% (Fierce Biotech, NEJM)Discontinuations clustered in dose escalation
EloraTZP (phase 2b)Most common, mostly mild or moderate10.8% to 27.0% across arms vs 2.9% tirzepatide alone (Lilly)Company-reported, not peer-reviewed
Petrelintide (ZUPREME-1)Described as comparable to placebo (Roche)Withdrawal for any reason 8.4% vs 13.6% placeboPhase 2 only
Aleniglipron (ACCESS)Not sourced here7.7% to 13.3% across doses (company)Phase 2b
Wegovy pill (OASIS 4), approved74.0% vs 42.2% placeboAbout 7%Empty-stomach dosing rule
Wegovy HD (STEP UP), approvedHigher than at 2.4 mgSee our dosing guideMore skin sensation problems at 7.2 mg (FDA, via Healio)

How to read that table

  • Discontinuation is the number that matters most. A side effect you tolerate is an inconvenience; one that makes you stop ends the treatment, and weight returns when treatment stops. Survodutide's phase 3 rate is the outlier.
  • Dose drives side effects as much as the drug does. Retatrutide's 4 mg dose had a lower adverse-event discontinuation rate than placebo; its 12 mg dose more than double. The same is true across the class.
  • Dysesthesia is new and seems tied to large effects. It appeared with retatrutide and with semaglutide 7.2 mg, in both cases more at higher doses. Nobody yet knows why.
  • Time's 40% figure is the context. Time reported that roughly 40% of people who start these drugs stop within a year. Real-world stopping is higher than trial stopping, because trials provide support and select motivated volunteers.

The standard warnings on the approved GLP-1 labels, covered in our semaglutide side-effects guide, will almost certainly appear on any approved pipeline GLP-1 drug as well. The final labels will say what else applies.

sections.heading: Can you get a pipeline drug now through a trial or a compounding pharmacy?
sections.body:
Only through a trial. There is no legal compounded version of any drug in this guide that is not approved, and no telehealth provider can legitimately prescribe one.

Compounding

Compounding pharmacies prepare medicines from active ingredients under specific legal conditions, and the compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide sold by telehealth providers are made from the ingredients of approved drugs. The FDA has stated that retatrutide and cagrilintide cannot be used in compounding under federal law, because they are not components of an approved drug. The same logic applies to every unapproved molecule here: amycretin, MariTide, survodutide, petrelintide, eloralintide, aleniglipron, bimagrumab. If you see "compounded retatrutide" or "compounded CagriSema" offered, it is not a lawful compounded product. Our compounded vs brand-name guide explains what questions to ask about compounded semaglutide, which is a different matter.

Clinical trials

The legitimate route to an unapproved drug is a registered trial. Several of the drugs above have trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, including the MARITIME-SWITCH trial, which specifically enrols people moving from a weekly GLP-1, and Lilly's eloralintide phase 3 trials. Trials have strict eligibility rules, many include a placebo arm so you may not receive the drug, and some exclude people currently on a GLP-1. If you are interested, the registry lists sites and contacts; your clinician can help judge whether a trial suits you.

Approved drugs abroad

Ecnoglutide is approved in China. That does not make it legal to import for personal use as a weight-loss treatment, and the same goes for any foreign-approved product sold online to US buyers.

The "research peptide" market

As covered above, the FDA has warned sellers of retatrutide and other GLP-1 products labelled "for research purposes". The label is a legal fiction, the content is unverified, and nobody is accountable for what is in the vial.

sections.heading: What will the new weight-loss drugs cost?
sections.body:
Nobody knows, and no company has published a US price for any pipeline drug in the sources we found. Scientific American's coverage of the coming drugs notes that prices for the current drugs remain high and insurance coverage can be limited or denied, which is the realistic starting assumption for the next ones too. Anything you read giving a "retatrutide price" or "CagriSema cost" for a legitimate US product is a guess, or a grey-market vial price, which is not the same thing.

What the approved options cost now

The figures below are copied from our verified price index and existing guides, with their conditions. They are the comparison any new drug will face.
